market_summary: Markets are in a risk-off mood: hotter-than-expected October CPI (0.4% vs 0.3% expected) sent the 10-year Treasury yield briefly above 5% on Nov 10, crushing rate-hike-sensitive tech and high-multiple growth names (S&P -0.4%, Nasdaq -0.7% on Tue). Nvidia is the standout casualty, down ~9.5% in a day and nearly $470B over two sessions after CEO Jensen Huang admitted an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, triggering a board investigation just before its Nov 17 earnings. In Singapore, Q3 bank earnings diverged sharply — OCBC beat while DBS and UOB missed — against a backdrop of NIM pressure, even as STI financials rallied on the day. Mega-cap tech earnings (Apple, Meta) were largely strong on fundamentals, but macro/rate fears and single-name scandal risk are currently overriding fundamentals in US tech.

picks.thesis: Nvidia is in the middle of an unresolved governance crisis (CEO affair with a suspected Chinese spy, board investigation ongoing) that has already wiped ~$470B in two sessions. Stock is down 9.5% in a single day with 3.9x normal volume, and earnings land Nov 17 — a high-risk event while the scandal narrative is still developing and rate-hike fears are hitting high-multiple AI names hardest. Momentum and headline risk both point lower into the print.
picks.news: CEO Jensen Huang admitted an affair with a suspected Chinese spy; board launched an investigation (Nov 8), stock fell 4.3% that day, then another 5.5% on Nov 10 as fallout deepened, for a combined ~$470B two-day wipeout; separately, hot CPI on Nov 10 pushed Fed hike odds up sharply, pressuring AI/data-center valuations (Cramer warning, Nov 10).
picks.risks: Board could quickly clear Huang or install reassuring governance changes; a strong Nov 17 earnings beat/guide could override the scandal narrative; analyst consensus target still implies ~93% upside, so a short squeeze on any positive headline is a real risk.

picks.thesis: Meta posted standout Q3 ad momentum (26% YoY revenue growth, ad impressions +10%, price/ad +14%) and the stock jumped 5.1% on the day with analysts still seeing ~32% upside to consensus target. Despite a rough past month (-10.8%) tied to broader tech de-rating, the underlying ad business is accelerating, which should support a recovery as rate-fear-driven selling fades.
picks.news: Meta Q3 2026 earnings (Nov 5) showed core advertising revenue up 26% YoY to $64.6B with rising ad prices and volumes; shares rallied +5.1% most recently as the market digested the strength.
picks.risks: If Treasury yields keep climbing on hawkish Fed repricing, high-beta/high-multiple names like Meta (beta 1.25, 41% annualized vol) could get hit again regardless of fundamentals; AI capex spending concerns could also resurface.

picks.thesis: OCBC beat Q3 2026 consensus with S$2.04B net profit while peers DBS and UOB missed, and the stock responded with the sharpest gain in the trio (+3.1%) on nearly 2x normal volume — a sign the market is rewarding the earnings differentiation. Longer-term uptrend (+57% over 1Y, +10.8% above 200-day MA) remains intact despite a recent pullback, and there's additional optionality from Singapore's growing role as an Asian gold-trading hub.
picks.news: OCBC Q3 2026 beat consensus (Nov 6) while DBS and UOB missed, widening the performance gap among Singapore banks; separate Nov 9 report flagged growing institutional interest in Singapore as an Asian gold hub, a tailwind for OCBC's wealth/precious metals franchise.
picks.risks: Sector-wide NIM compression from potential rate cuts could still weigh on OCBC's margins even if it's outperforming peers; a broader SGX risk-off move (STI financials are volatile, rel. volume elevated) could drag it down with the group.

picks.thesis: UOB missed Q3 2026 consensus, the weakest of the three Singapore banks, and its price action confirms the underperformance: worst 1-month (-6.5%), 3-month (-10.9%) and from-52w-high (-16.8%) readings among the local banks, trading below both its 50- and 200-day moving averages. Analyst sentiment has also cooled, with a notably higher hold/sell mix (9 hold, 2 sell out of 16) versus OCBC and DBS.
picks.news: UOB missed Q3 2026 estimates (reported Nov 6) amid sector-wide NIM pressure, underperforming OCBC which beat.
picks.risks: UOB still has a positive implied upside to consensus target (+10.4%) and any rebound in regional rate-cut expectations or bank sector re-rating could lift all three SGX banks together, including UOB.

picks.thesis: Hotter-than-expected October CPI pushed the 10-year yield above 5% and collapsed December rate-cut odds (CME FedWatch down to 3% from 21%), a direct headwind for the high-multiple, long-duration tech names that dominate QQQ. The Nasdaq-100 is already down 10.2% over the past month and sits 11.2% below its 52-week high, with Nvidia's ongoing scandal adding an idiosyncratic drag to a major index constituent right before its Nov 17 earnings.
picks.news: October CPI came in at 0.4% vs 0.3% expected (Nov 10), triggering a surge in Treasury yields and a sharp repricing of Fed hike odds; Nasdaq fell 0.7% the same day amid the broader tech-led selloff.
picks.risks: A one-day 2.8% bounce already occurred, suggesting markets may be looking past the CPI print quickly; strong mega-cap earnings (Meta, Apple) could offset macro weakness and drive QQQ higher despite rate concerns.

picks.thesis: Keppel has very strong analyst support (12 buy, 2 hold, 1 sell; +30.2% implied upside to consensus target) despite poor recent momentum (-7.2% 1m, -13.6% 3m, 25.9% below 52w high), suggesting the market may be overly pessimistic relative to fundamentals. The 3.3% single-day pop on elevated volume could be the start of a bounce off oversold technical levels.
picks.news: No fresh company-specific catalyst identified in the latest news gathering; this is a valuation/analyst-gap view based on price stats alone, so conviction is low and should be treated as speculative given the lack of recent news confirmation.
picks.risks: Elevated volatility (25.1% annualized, beta 1.15) and no specific positive catalyst mean the stock could continue its downtrend if broader SGX sentiment stays weak; without a known catalyst, the analyst-target gap could simply reflect stale targets rather than genuine upside.
